## Understand language models, one mechanism at a time

A navigable learning map that synthesizes strong explanations from research papers, rigorous books, official documentation, and visual teaching resources. Start with the whole system, then follow only the concepts or details that answer your current question. High-level pages explain how components work together; concept pages offer deeper explanations without making every derivation a prerequisite.

The long-term goal is to understand and build a small decoder-only autoregressive language model, using inspectable components and tests. The goal is a coherent, original synthesis—not a copy of any one book: sources are selected for what they establish or explain well, then connected through consistent notation, explicit assumptions, counterexamples, and evidence. Sebastian Raschka's repository is a major source and comparison point, not a table of contents to copy or evidence that the corresponding steps are already implemented here.

## Start here

For a first pass, read these two lessons in order:

1. **Represent text** — [tokens, token IDs, and BPE](text-data.qmd).
2. **Understand the objective** — [input-target shifting, windows, and masks](training-examples.qmd).

Then continue with the suggested path below. Pages connect intuition, equations, and code; the roadmap distinguishes available explanations from implementations that have actually been tested.

## Choose your depth

You do not have to read every page in order. Use the overview to understand a mechanism's role; open a concept page when you want its details; follow implementation, tests, or papers when you want to verify or investigate it. Essential prerequisites are signposted, while related topics are optional routes.

For example, you can understand why a Transformer needs positional information without deriving **RoPE**. The [positional-encoding page](positional-encoding.qmd) offers the geometry, derivation, implementation considerations, and limitations when those details become useful.

## Suggested path

1. **From text to tokens** — Unicode, encoding, tokenization, BPE, and reference resources. [Open the lesson](text-data.qmd).
2. **Data and the autoregressive objective** — context windows, input-target shifting, batching, and loss masking. [Open the lesson](training-examples.qmd).
3. **Maths applied to LLMs** — follow logits through the training loss and gradients without duplicating a general mathematics course.
4. **Attention and Transformers** — queries, keys, values, scores, softmax, positional information (including RoPE), and causal masking.
5. **Model and training** — blocks, optimization, validation, generation, and evaluation.
6. **Critical notes** — examine assumptions, counterexamples, and the limitations of metrics and representations.

This path describes the learning structure, not the implementation status of every component. The [detailed learning path](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md), [full curriculum and source-coverage plan](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/full-curriculum-plan.md), and [roadmap](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md) define the learning stages, how sources fit the project, and validation criteria respectively.

## How to use the sources

Different resources serve different purposes: an animation can build intuition, a research paper establishes the original formulation, official documentation specifies API behaviour, and tested code checks a defined property. Cross-check them rather than treating them as interchangeable.

- [Sebastian Raschka — reading recommendations](https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch/blob/main/ch01/reading-recommendations.md): first read for the big picture, second read with code, then critical reuse in a project.
- [3Blue1Brown — Transformers, the tech behind LLMs](https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/gpt/): visual intuition for data flow and LLM components.
- [Jay Alammar — The Illustrated Transformer](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-transformer/) and [The Illustrated GPT-2](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-gpt2/): visual walkthroughs of architectures; distinguish the original encoder-decoder Transformer from a decoder-only GPT.
- [Hugging Face — LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/): a structured supplement for concepts, tools, and models.

Formal references and further resources are collected in the [annotated bibliography](../references.qmd). For each page, mathematical and technical claims should be connected to an appropriate source; pedagogical links support understanding but do not replace definitions, assumptions, or derivations.
